note: Criterion 3 of the @solid-primitives checkpoint (docs/package-contract-v2/phase22/2026-09-28-solid-primitives-checkpoint.md). Each case is compiled and checked against the real published package at the version scripts/ecosystem-benchmark/primitives-checkpoint-corpus.json pins, installed with the head probe's Solid runtime, never against a stub. `misuse` must report `rule` as `kind` (default `violation`; `uncertifiable` where the certified summary states the export only may register -- every owner-requirement count `min: 0`, ADR 0161 -- and a violation there is an overclaim); `correct` must report nothing; `tsc` must be silent on both. Run with `make primitives-checkpoint` or `bun scripts/primitives-checkpoint.mjs --misuse`.

cases.why: No authored contract covers the none or node host, and the certified summary these hosts once had stated owner requirements whose every count is `min: 0` (ADR 0161). Called at module scope, with no owner, that is a proof obligation, not a proven leak, and is reported uncertifiable.
cases.misuse:
import { createTimer } from "@solid-primitives/timer";

createTimer(() => console.log("tick"), 1000, setInterval);

cases.why: In the browser build `isServer` is false, so createTimer always registers its interval cleanup on the ambient owner; the authored contract states that cleanup with `min: 1` and a required owner, and Chrome on rc.13 raises the missing-owner warning for this call. Called at module scope there is no owner, so the timer is never disposed.

Called at module scope, with no owner, that is a proof obligation, not a proven leak, and is reported uncertifiable.
cases.misuse:
import { keyArray } from "@solid-primitives/keyed";

keyArray(() => [1, 2], item => item, value => value());

cases.why: In the browser build `isServer` is false, so keyArray always registers its cleanup on the ambient owner; the authored contract states that, and Chrome on rc.13 raises NO_OWNER_CLEANUP for this call (with `@solid-primitives/utils` installed by the app, which keyed imports but does not declare). Called at module scope there is no owner, so the mapping is never disposed.
cases.misuse:
import { keyArray } from "@solid-primitives/keyed";

keyArray(() => [1, 2], item => item, value => value());

cases.why: tap's body calls `onCleanup(() => cleanup?.())` before anything can return, so its certified summary states the cleanup with `min: 1`: every call registers (ADR 0161). Called at module scope there is no owner, so the cleanup has nowhere to register and the pointer listeners the returned directive adds are never removed.

import { tap } from "@solid-primitives/gestures";

export const onTap = tap({ callback: position => console.log(position.x, position.y) });
